issues.problem: The stated overall threshold of 10 follows the earlier Horizon Europe rules. The standard overall threshold for full RIA/IA proposals under the 2026–2027 Work Programme is 12 out of 15.
issues.fix: Change the overall threshold to 12 and cite the applicable provision in the dated 2026–2027 General Annexes.

issues.problem: The YAML permits a 3% tolerance, while the public call states an absolute 18,000-word limit and says excess text is disregarded. A 3% allowance amounts to 540 additional words and is undisclosed.
issues.fix: Set tolerance to zero, or state the exact tolerance and its enforcement in call.md so both files define identical treatment.

issues.problem: The cost-table instructions misstate the standard actual-cost template. The 15% personnel-cost trigger concerns purchase costs, not all 'other direct costs'. Subcontracting and other applicable cost categories have separate reporting requirements that this purportedly exact template omits.
issues.fix: Reproduce the applicable standard template's table requirements and conditional instructions, distinguishing purchase costs, subcontracting, other cost categories and applicable in-kind contributions. Apply the 15% trigger per participant to purchase costs.

issues.where: call.md, call conditions and Sources; call.yaml
issues.problem: No submission deadline is supplied. The call therefore lacks a usable submission schedule and cannot establish compliance with the requirement that deadlines fall after 1 October 2026.
issues.fix: Add an invented deadline after 1 October 2026, including time and time zone, record it consistently in both files, and include dates in the fictional-call declaration.

issues.where: call.md, Scope and Specific conditions; call.yaml, SC3, SC4, ME1 and ME3
issues.problem: Several answer-key items combine independently satisfiable requirements. SC4 combines socio-economic impact assessment with comparative cost-effectiveness evaluation; ME1 combines data management, publication access and access to data and tools; ME3 combines three distinct SSH contributions. SC3 similarly combines an adoption route with two different governance outputs. A proposal can satisfy only part of each item, making a single compliance judgment ambiguous.
issues.fix: Split these into separately identifiable requirements in both files, preserving the intended obligations and any conditional wording.

issues.where: call.md, Specific conditions, open science bullet; call.yaml, ME1
issues.problem: 'Where possible, data and tools' leaves the condition for withholding outputs undefined. It also obscures the distinction between mandatory Horizon Europe research-data obligations and optional openness of other outputs.
issues.fix: State the applicable FAIR data-management and open-access obligations, including permitted data-access exceptions and their justification. State separately whether open release of tools is mandatory, conditional or encouraged.

issues.problem: The sources do not identify the versions supporting the claimed exact fidelity. One link is a general reference-document landing page and the other is a mutable application-template URL. This is particularly consequential when combining a 2026–2027 page limit with scoring and template instructions that may come from earlier versions.
issues.fix: Cite the exact General Annexes document and the application form's version and date, with relevant sections or pages. Reconcile the complete section list, including the status of the impact-summary table, against that same applicable template.
